title: epoch-based-temp-allocator-and-kv-delta-merge
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: peak GPU memory usage during long sequences and high-concurrency workloads is dominated by transient scratch allocations and aggressive KV cache snapshots. This PR introduces an epoch-based temporary allocator that collects per-request transient allocations into epoch buckets and frees them deterministically at epoch boundaries, plus a KV delta-merge flow that stores incremental KV updates instead of full snapshots for most roll-forward paths. The goals are to reduce peak workspace footprint, lower allocation churn, and shrink KV snapshot hotset pressure so that scheduling and batching are more effective.

What this changes (single continuous description): - epoch allocator: EpochManager, EpochBuffer, and a lock-free freelist for short-lived tensors; allocates small scratch segments from per-GPU arenas and defers global coalescing until safe epochs. - temp allocation heuristics: heuristics to fold per-step scratch into existing activations when lifetime shorter than batch window. - KV delta merge: captures writes to KV in append-only deltas and applies a compact merge at checkpoint time instead of taking a full shadow copy for every request. - scheduler integration: small changes to the work-stealing scheduler to prefer tasks that can reuse epoch buffers and avoid preempting tasks with large pinned allocations. - runtime flags (off by default for Dedicated): runtime.allocator.epoch.enabled, runtime.kv.delta_merge.enabled, and tuning knobs for epoch length and delta flush thresholds.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked in Linear (ENG-1679) [x] unit tests for allocator lifecycle and KV delta application [x] microbench marker tests for memory high-water and allocation counts [x] e2e perf job against canary model suite [ ] docs: will follow up with a short Ops note in the Console docs.

Compatibility and migration: This is backward compatible. If runtime.allocator.epoch.enabled=false, behavior is unchanged. Delta-merge has a compatibility shim to interoperate with old full-snapshot readers; we fall back to full snapshot for models that require byte-exact KV semantics (legacy modes).

Testing and results: Benchmarking on a 4xA100 cluster using the long-seq translation workload (seq=4096, batched arrival) shows: - median peak GPU memory per worker reduced by ~18% - 95th-percentile allocation churn down by 36% - average request latency unchanged (+0.8% median) - throughput at 99th-percentile latency SLO improved by ~6% in continuous-batching mode. Canary results run for 72 hours with no regression alerts.

Risk and rollback: The main risk is a pathological workload that pins epoch buffers for long-lived requests; to mitigate, epoch length defaults to a conservative 100ms and there is a hard cap on retained epoch memory. Rollback is trivial via feature flags; a quick toggle will revert both allocator and KV delta behavior.

Operational notes: Added Prometheus metrics: epoch_alloc_bytes, epoch_retained_bytes, kv_delta_bytes, kv_delta_apply_latency. Added a tracing span for delta-merge.apply so we can correlate merge cost to request latency.

Related work: builds on earlier arena and checkpoint improvements (ENG-1452, see related PRs) but takes a different approach by grouping transient allocations temporally and reducing KV snapshot surface area.
